slots.speaker: Tamara Molyarova
slots.title: Chemistry and Radial Drift Shape the Composition of Protoplanetary Discs
slots.abstract: The chemical composition of protoplanetary discs traces their physical conditions and the processes shaping their evolution. Recent JWST observations reveal a diversity of inner disc compositions, as well as correlations with system properties, such as stellar mass and age, accretion rate, and the presence of substructures. These correlations have been attributed to dust radial drift bringing ice-rich material from the outer disc regions. In this work, I model dust evolution and radial drift in a protoplanetary disc together with chemical reactions across a range of disc properties, and show how chemical evolution can modify the impact of radial drift on the inner disc composition over timescales of a few Myr. I predict correlations between observable disc properties and chemical composition, and compare these predictions with existing JWST observations.

slots.speaker: David Wands
slots.title: Primordial black holes from stochastic inflation
slots.abstract: The idea that primordial black holes could form from large density perturbations in the early radiation-dominated universe has intrigued cosmologists since the idea was proposed by Carr and Hawking in the 1970s. They could in principle have a wide range of masses with a wide range of astrophysical effects, and there has been a resurgence of interest in the era of gravitational wave astronomy with the idea that we might be able to directly detect primordial black holes through their gravitational radiation produced either when they form or in binary mergers. Primordial density perturbations, as observed for example in the cosmic microwave background radiation, are thought to originate from microscopic quantum fluctuations during inflation, a period of accelerated expansion in the very early universe before the radiation-dominated era. Inflation generates primordial density perturbations on all cosmic scales, but until recently it has mainly been studied in the context of semi-classical, slow-roll inflation leading to small almost scale-invariant, almost Gaussian density perturbations on the largest observable scales. I will discuss recent work exploring large,  nonlinear, fluctuations during inflation which could provide the seeds for the formation of primordial black holes. In particular I will present results from a stochastic description of inflation used to model the non-Gaussian distribution of rare, but large primordial perturbations and some of the challenges going beyond the semi-classical, slow-roll regime.

slots.speaker: Stuart Bale
slots.title: The Parker Solar Probe mission: What we have learned from our first visit to a star
slots.abstract: The NASA Parker Solar Probe (PSP) mission was launched in 2018 and has made 29 orbits of the Sun with perihelion altitudes down to 8.9 solar radii above the solar photosphere. An increasingly plausible picture is emerging of where the solar wind originates, how it is initially energized, and the plasma physics of the extended wind heating process. In this scenario, the fast solar wind originates by magnetic reconnection at intense bundles of field energy associated with the supergranulation convection cells. The emerging wind generates Alfvén waves, by the reconnection process, shearing instabilities, or phase speed gradients. These Alfvén waves grow to large amplitude dB/B~1 by a combination of plasma expansion and conservation of wave action. The large nonlinear Alfvén waves generate small scale turbulence that results in plasma wave heating, which provides the thermal energy to counteract the cooling of expansion. I will review some of the key PSP results that underpin this scenario and I will show some new results indicating the origin of 'slow' solar wind.
